findings.description: An AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with repository access, Terraform state access, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve these long-lived credentials and impersonate the associated IAM principal.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables holding secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key, with no customer-controlled key policy or separate boundary limiting who can decrypt them.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which is end-of-life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet-level egress controls — a ready exfiltration path given the credentials stored in its environment.
